raw_case_text:
The patient is an 18-year-old African American male hospitalized for elevated serum creatinine (2.74 mg/dL) and nephrotic syndrome. Serological evaluation revealed negative anti-nuclear antibody, anti-dsDNA, c-ANCA, p-ANCA, hepatitis B and C antibodies, HIV, and anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody. Complement C3 and C4 levels were normal, and serum free light chain ratio was not elevated or suppressed. Kidney biopsy revealed morphological findings of CG (Figure 1). PB19 viral load was elevated at 96,600 IU/mL. There were no recent respiratory infections or history of recurrent infections as a child. He was given 2 g/kg IVIg in an attempt to treat the PB19. His initial viral load increased to 107,000 IU/mL but then subsequently decreased to 800 IU/mL by November 2017. Despite the reduction in PB19 titer, his kidney function rapidly decreased and he was initiated on dialysis. He began evaluation for kidney transplantation, and a non-related African American living donor was identified. 
In an attempt to eradicate the PB19 infection before transplantation he was given 2 more courses of 2 g/kg IVIg over the next 4 months. His viral load remained positive at low levels. Further immunologic evaluation was negative except for low mannan-binding lectin (< 70 ng/mL, normal > 100). PB19 IgG was positive, but PB19 IgM was negative. Genetic testing found the patient to be heterozygous for APOL1 G1/G2 alleles. A second attempt to eradicate the PB19 viremia began with cidofovir treatment based on published in vitro efficacy. The patient received cidofovir 0.5 mg/kg every 2 weeks as suggested by a pharmacologic study of cidofovir in patients with kidney disease. He received a total of 7 doses of cidofovir before PB19 viral load became negative. As his donor was available for a limited window of time, it was decided to proceed with living donor transplantation after administering the 8th dose of cidofovir. Five days after the 8th dose of cidofovir, he received a living unrelated kidney transplant. Induction immunosuppression included methylprednisolone 500 mg at the time of surgery and basiliximab on post-operative day (POD) 0 and 4. He was maintained on tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and corticosteroids were tapered to prednisone 5 mg daily over 5 days. Due to the intense immunosuppression associated with induction, the patient was given a 9th dose of cidofovir on post-operative day 2 (7 days from the previous dose of cidofovir). Creatinine immediately decreased following transplant but then increased by POD 4. PB19 viral load was repeated and found to be positive at 1,100 IU/mL. Subsequently, a kidney biopsy was performed on POD 5 which revealed a Banff grade 2a rejection. As there was no evidence of CG on biopsy but clear vascular rejection, the clinical team decided that the risk of worsening PB19 viral replication by aggressive treatment of rejection was outweighed by the clear negative impact of ongoing rejection. Therefore the patient was treated with 10 mg/kg of rabbit antithymocyte globulin and steroid bolus. Kidney function improved, and a repeat kidney biopsy 2 weeks after treatment revealed mild acute tubular injury and no evidence of CG or podocyte effacement. Repeat PB19 viral load 1 month later revealed a decrease in PCR to the lower limit of laboratory testing < 199 IU/mL. The kinetics of PB19 viremia from the time of diagnosis to 6 weeks after transplantation is seen in Figure 2. Other viruses including cytomegalovirus and polyoma (BK) virus were not detected. Ten months post transplant his creatinine is 2 mg/dL, and there is no proteinuria. PB19 has remained detected but < 199 IU/mL up to 6 months post transplant after which it has no longer been tested.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 18-year-old African American male presented with elevated serum creatinine (2.74 mg/dL) and nephrotic syndrome secondary to human parvovirus B19-associated collapsing glomerulopathy, progressing to end-stage renal disease requiring kidney transplantation.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Hospitalized with acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.74 mg/dL) and nephrotic syndrome without preceding respiratory illness, the patient was found to have collapsing glomerulopathy (CG), APOL1 G1/G2 heterozygosity, and parvovirus B19 (PB19) viremia (96,600 IU/mL). Despite three courses of high-dose IVIG (2 g/kg each), his renal function deteriorated to dialysis dependence while low-level PB19 viremia persisted. To clear PB19 prior to living-unrelated kidney transplantation, he received 8 biweekly doses of renal-adjusted intravenous cidofovir (0.5 mg/kg q2w, clearing PB19 after dose 7) and underwent kidney transplantation 5 days after dose 8 (with a 9th cidofovir dose on POD 2), complicated on POD 4-5 by acute creatinine rise and low-level PB19 rebound (1,100 IU/mL).
subjective.past_medical_history: Parvovirus B19-associated collapsing glomerulopathy progressing to ESRD on hemodialysis; heterozygous carrier of APOL1 G1/G2 risk alleles; low mannan-binding lectin (<70 ng/mL); no history of recurrent childhood infections.
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial nephrotic syndrome edema/proteinuria; no recent respiratory infections.

objective.routine_investigations: Initial serum creatinine 2.74 mg/dL with nephrotic-range proteinuria; negative ANA, anti-dsDNA, c-ANCA, p-ANCA, HBV, HCV, HIV, and anti-GBM antibodies; normal C3, C4, and serum free light chain ratio; low mannan-binding lectin (<70 ng/mL, normal >100); PB19 IgG positive, PB19 IgM negative. Post-transplant creatinine improved immediately then rose on POD 4 (stabilizing at 2.0 mg/dL with no proteinuria at 10 months post-transplant).
objective.advanced_workup: Genetic testing showed compound heterozygosity for APOL1 G1/G2 alleles. Native kidney biopsy demonstrated collapsing glomerulopathy (CG). Quantitative blood parvovirus B19 (PB19) PCR was 96,600 IU/mL at presentation (peaking at 107,000 IU/mL, dropping to 800 IU/mL after IVIG, becoming undetectable after 7 doses of cidofovir, transiently rebounding to 1,100 IU/mL on POD 4, and remaining <199 IU/mL at 1 and 6 months post-transplant); cytomegalovirus (CMV) and BK polyomavirus were not detected. POD 5 renal allograft biopsy revealed Banff grade 2a acute vascular rejection without collapsing glomerulopathy; repeat allograft biopsy 2 weeks after rabbit ATG and steroid bolus showed only mild acute tubular injury without CG or podocyte effacement.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with parvovirus B19-associated collapsing glomerulopathy in an APOL1 G1/G2 heterozygous patient leading to ESRD, successfully bridged to living-unrelated kidney transplantation using pre-transplant IVIG (2 g/kg x 3 courses) and biweekly low-dose intravenous cidofovir (0.5 mg/kg every 2 weeks x 9 total doses; CMV and BK virus negative). Post-transplant POD 5 Banff grade 2a acute vascular rejection (with transient PB19 rebound to 1,100 IU/mL) was treated with rabbit antithymocyte globulin (10 mg/kg) and corticosteroid bolus alongside tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone (5 mg daily), achieving suppression of PB19 viremia to <199 IU/mL and stable allograft function (creatinine 2.0 mg/dL without proteinuria) at 10 months post-transplant.
